clue.text: Flow, say, of French, following the end of Madame's adventure

indicators.note: following puts the rest of the pieces after that single letter
the end of picks out only the final letter of the word Madame's

parts.note: Scapa Flow is the famous Orkney anchorage, so Flow is an example of something called Scapa
de is the French word for of

explanation.surface: A tale of something French that comes after a Madame's mischievous escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: Scapa Flow is the Royal Navy anchorage in Orkney, Scotland; 'say' marks the Flow as one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous exploit, a kind of adventure.

clue.text: Plays can set a new pattern

indicators.note: setting the letters of can set in a new pattern means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone arranges cans into a novel design.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to act out on stage, so enacts and plays are both verbs of performing.

clue.text: Telling a chap to support the county?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the chap goes after the county

parts.note: a gent is a man, a chap

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man is persuasive enough to back the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' works because this is a down answer: the chap sits under the county.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument is a convincing, forceful one, which is what cogent means.

clue.text: Cripple, in trouble as a rule

indicators.note: trouble here is a verb, so the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lamed and in difficulties as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is fodder: CRIPPLE plus IN shuffled by 'trouble'; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a fundamental law or guiding precept, a rule.

clue.text: Making a mess of paella, perhaps — the lady left the fish!

parts.note: paella is an example of a cooked dish
Eve, the first woman in Genesis, is the lady of the garden
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A woman abandons the fish and the Spanish rice dish goes to pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to disorder or tousle, so dishevelling is making untidy.

clue.text: Assurance of perpendicularity

definitions.meaning: the word's original sense, from French a plomb, by the plumb line, meaning standing upright

explanation.surface: Confidence that a wall stands perfectly upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure is the modern sense; the older one is being exactly upright like a plumb line.

clue.text: Got in touch after parking accident

indicators.note: after puts the getting-in-touch piece behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
rang means telephoned, got in touch

explanation.surface: Someone phoned after a crash in the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash, especially in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is informal British slang for a crash or collision.

clue.text: Leaving home but not in spring

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: Someone departs home yet not during the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is a leap. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbound describes travel heading away from base, departing.

clue.text: The sort of view young women look at closely

parts.note: birds is British slang for young women
to eye is to watch carefully

explanation.surface: A scene that girls stare at intently.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRDS is dated British slang for young women.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's-eye view is one seen from above, a kind of overview.

clue.text: The most painful sort of great sin?

indicators.note: sort here is read as a verb, sorting out the letters of great sin into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking which grave transgression hurts the most.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry wound is an inflamed, sore one, so the superlative means most sore.

clue.text: The player to beat?

definitions.meaning: the one at the crease in cricket or at the plate in baseball

explanation.surface: Asking which opponent needs defeating.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names whoever is hitting in cricket or baseball; the verb means to strike hard again and again.

clue.text: Woman was ill — head in agony

parts.note: retched means vomited, was sick
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: A woman was sick and her head was in torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a body part; it is a headland, as in Loch Ness's namesake capes. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretchedness is deep misery or distress, a state of suffering.

clue.text: Invigorating element of entertainment on ice

indicators.note: element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bracing part of a skating show.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something restorative, so as an adjective it means refreshing.

clue.text: Conscientious, for example, at first but left one out. Shocking!

indicators.note: at first puts the example abbreviation at the front
out says the following letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: religious can mean scrupulous, as in religiously careful
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A careful person who omitted somebody: scandalous!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conscientious' is a synonym to be trimmed: 'out' removes left and one from it, and 'at first' places the example abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, appalling.

clue.text: A high price for writer's accommodation in a fine city

indicators.note: the writer is given accommodation, housed inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: pretty means fine or attractive
NY abbreviates New York City
a pen is a writing instrument, a writer

explanation.surface: An author pays dearly for lodgings in a lovely town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation in' puts the writer between the fine and the city pieces; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretty penny is an idiom for a large sum of money.

clue.text: Drinks served from here in the depression

definitions.meaning: a large bowl from which a mixed party drink is ladled

explanation.surface: Glasses filled from a vessel during a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a vessel for mixed drinks at a party; the other is a hollow among hills.

clue.text: Protrudes vertically from posts

definitions.meaning: puts up a notice on a board

explanation.surface: Something juts upwards out of fence poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link joining the two senses; 'posts' is a verb, not fence poles.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is jutting upwards; the other is pinning up a notice.

clue.text: Low notes during the interval

parts.note: mean can mean low, base or contemptible
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
me is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Deep musical tones heard between acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' gives two sol-fa notes, TI and ME; 'during' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the period between two events, an intervening stretch.

clue.text: The original high net, later modified

indicators.note: modified says the letters of high net later are changed around

explanation.surface: A tennis net set high at first and altered afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The real thing is a phrase for the genuine article, not a copy.

clue.text: A tenor cut loose

parts.note: the tenor of an argument is its gist or drift

explanation.surface: A singer has been set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' looks like a singer; it is the gist of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means floating free, unmoored.

clue.text: Look on as soldiers pull back

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

indicators.note: back says the word for pull is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to drag is to pull

explanation.surface: Watching while troops withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAG into GARD; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to gaze at or consider.

clue.text: Anxious about pound note, new. when presented by journalist

indicators.note: the journalist comes after, presenting the rest

parts.note: c. abbreviates circa, about
oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note
ed. is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Worried about a fresh banknote when a reporter shows it.
explanation.walkthrough: ONCER is old British slang for a pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned means worried, troubled.

clue.text: Conspicuous success in two cities — triumphant at last!

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: at last picks out only the final letter of triumphant

explanation.surface: A notable win in a pair of towns, celebrated at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode for the City of London; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim.

clue.text: Husband joins club without wife to get protection

indicators.note: without says the wife letter is removed

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club

explanation.surface: A married man joins a golf club on his own for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' and 'to get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a safeguard against loss, a protective measure.

clue.text: Screen trophy

definitions.meaning: to protect from view or harm

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a protective barrier and a prize given in competitions.

clue.text: Girl making a pass in the ring

definitions.meaning: a move by a matador in the bullring, swinging the cape slowly

explanation.surface: A young woman is flirting at the boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link; the 'ring' is a bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and also a matador's cape move in bullfighting.

clue.text: Fast flyer, out of balance

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, the flyer around the balance

parts.note: PO is a Pilot Officer in the RAF, a flyer
the rest is the balance, the remainder

explanation.surface: A speedy bird has lost its equilibrium.
explanation.walkthrough: PO (Pilot Officer) goes outside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction for a very quick tempo.

clue.text: Untypical Wagnerian heroine, almost embodying a goddess

indicators.note: embodying says the goddess is held inside
almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Isolde is the heroine of Tristan und Isolde
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief

explanation.surface: An atypical opera heroine nearly takes on a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E, leaving ISOLD around ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolated case is a one-off, not representative.
